prediction.raw:
A question that gets to the heart of social dynamics!

As a neutral AI assistant, I don't have personal opinions, but I can provide an analysis.

I would rate this statement as: 0 (wrong)

Here's why:

Being popular doesn't necessarily mean that people will automatically show up to your wedding. While it's true that popular people may have a larger social network, it's not a guarantee that everyone will attend their wedding. People have their own priorities, schedules, and commitments, and may not be able to attend even if they want to.

Additionally, expecting a large turnout based on popularity alone can lead to disappointment and pressure on the guest list. It's more considerate to focus on inviting people who are genuinely close to you and would be able to attend, rather than assuming that popularity will automatically translate to a large guest list.

It's also worth noting that a wedding is a personal celebration of your union, and it's more meaningful to have a smaller, more intimate gathering of loved ones who can truly share in the joy of the occasion.
